research.report:
# Tom Müller of revel8: Publicly Documented Professional Activities

## Scope and identification

This report concerns **Tom C. Müller**, identified by revel8 as its co-founder and product lead, and by a company-profile database as a co-founder and co-CEO. The strongest link between the name and the role is revel8’s own author profile, which says that Müller leads product development. Tracxn calls “Tom Muller” a co-founder and CEO, but revel8’s supplied author profile uses the more specific title **“Co-Founder & Product.”** Accordingly, “co-CEO” is treated here as a reported title rather than an independently established description of his day-to-day remit. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom); [Tracxn, 2026](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/revel8/__y_4-TRqdVfYL7aJoS3_pcFUgSev2HB6U6ZT_96HodDY))

The source material also contains profiles of people with similar names: **Thomas Müller**, an automotive technology executive at JLR; **Tom Mueller**, a SpaceX co-founder; and **Tom Mueller**, a crisis-communications professional. None of those profiles establishes a connection to revel8’s product leader, and their careers are **not** attributed to him in this report. ([JLR, n.d.](https://media.jlr.com/corporate/person/thomas-muller); [YouTube, n.d.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SVH9IS5a4ss); [*The Leading in a Crisis Podcast*, n.d.](https://www.leadinginacrisis.com/2175298/contributors/53730-tom-mueller))

**Assessment:** The documented record supports a clear account of Müller’s work on revel8’s cybersecurity-awareness product and his authorship of company articles. It does **not** support a detailed pre-revel8 résumé, a list of conference talks, or claims that he personally developed particular underlying technologies. This distinction matters because descriptions of a company’s platform are not, by themselves, evidence of one founder’s individual technical contribution. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom); [revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

## Professional background and responsibilities

### Founding and prior experience

Revel8 identifies Müller as one of its three founders, alongside Julius Muth and Robert Seilbeck. Its funding announcement describes the founders as **Celonis alumni**, which supports a prior professional association with Celonis but gives no dates, job title, reporting line, or description of Müller’s individual work there. A separate September 2025 funding report likewise names the same three founders. No more detailed employment history should be inferred from those statements. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m))

Public sources disagree on **when revel8 was founded**. Revel8’s own announcement says **2024**, while Vestbee says it was launched in **2023**; a Startup.eu entry gives a **2026** founding date while also listing a September 2025 financing round. Because those accounts cannot all be correct, this report does not assign a definitive founding year. The consistent, better-supported point is that Müller is publicly named as a founder and that the company had announced seed financing by September 2025. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m); [Startup.eu, n.d.](https://www.startup.eu/startup/revel8))

### Product leadership

Revel8’s biography says Müller **leads product development** and is responsible for translating real-world attacker techniques into simulations and interactive training. It specifically names open-source-intelligence-based targeting, multichannel phishing, AI-powered voice phishing (“vishing”), and deepfakes as techniques relevant to that remit. This is direct evidence of his *stated responsibility*; it does not identify the software components he wrote, the teams he managed, or the date each capability entered the product. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom))

The company describes its broader offering as combining AI-powered attack simulations, OSINT-driven personalization, multichannel attack chains, and real-time micro-training. Vestbee describes simulations delivered through **email, SMS, voice, and video**. Taken together, these sources place Müller’s documented product role at the intersection of simulated social-engineering attacks and employee training. They should not be read as independent validation of the product’s effectiveness or as attribution of every feature solely to Müller. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m); [revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom))

## Publicly announced projects and product direction

| Documented activity | What the sources establish | Attribution limit |
|---|---|---|
| **Social-engineering simulations and interactive training** | Revel8 assigns Müller responsibility for turning attacker techniques into simulations and training experiences. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) | The profile describes a remit, not an individual engineering changelog. |
| **OSINT-informed, multichannel scenarios** | Revel8 describes OSINT personalization and multichannel attack chains; Vestbee identifies email, SMS, voice, and video as channels. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m)) | These are company and press descriptions of the platform, not published test results. |
| **AI impersonation training** | Müller’s company biography explicitly connects his product remit to AI-powered vishing and deepfake simulations. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) | The supplied material does not date a specific launch or demonstrate individual feature ownership. |
| **Enterprise and international expansion** | Revel8 says its newly announced funding would support product development, stronger enterprise features, team growth, and international expansion. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks)) | These are announced uses of capital and plans, not proof that each expansion milestone was completed. |
| **STACKIT marketplace availability** | Menlo Times reports that revel8 is among cybersecurity providers on the STACKIT marketplace. ([*Menlo Times*, n.d.](https://www.menlotimes.com/post/revel8-levels-up-its-fight-against-ai-powered-cyberattacks)) | The supplied report gives no launch date or evidence that Müller personally negotiated or built the integration. |

The company states a goal of training **10 million “human firewalls.”** That is a stated ambition, not a reported count of people trained. Similarly, references to compliance requirements such as **NIS2 and ISO 27001** describe how revel8 positions its offering; the supplied sources do not establish that Müller personally performed compliance work or that use of the product alone satisfies either framework. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

## Published technical and professional writing

Revel8’s author page credits Müller with the articles below. These are **dated company-published articles** on cybersecurity training and social-engineering topics. The supplied excerpts provide titles, dates, categories, and reading-time labels, but not the full articles. They therefore establish his public authorship and subject-matter focus—not the methodology, originality, or peer-reviewed status of any technical claims within the articles. All dates and titles in the table are reported by the author page. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom))

| Publication date | Article credited to Müller | Documented topic |
|---|---|---|
| July 23, 2026 | “CEO Fraud Losses in Germany: Real Costs, Cases and Prevention” | CEO-fraud cases and prevention. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |
| July 26, 2026 | “AiTM Proxy-Phishing: How Token Theft Defeats MFA” | Adversary-in-the-middle phishing and multifactor-authentication token theft. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |
| August 25, 2026 | “US Vendor vs. DACH Solution: NIS2 Decision Matrix” | Vendor selection and NIS2-related considerations. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |

| September 9, 2026 | “What Is OSINT-Based Social Engineering Training?” | OSINT-based training. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |
| September 11, 2026 | “revel8 vs. Hoxhunt: An Honest Comparison for DACH Enterprises” | A company-published vendor comparison. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |
| September 16, 2026 | “revel8 vs. Hornetsecurity: M365 vs. Multi-Channel OSINT” | A company-published comparison of training approaches. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |
| September 21, 2026 | “Phishing Simulation Costs 2026: What Drives the Price and the Hidden Costs” | Phishing-simulation pricing considerations. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |
| November 14, 2026 | “Best Security Awareness Training Providers in DACH (2026): Platforms Compared” | A regional vendor comparison. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom)) |

The **July 26 AiTM proxy-phishing article** is the most explicitly technical title in this supplied publication list. The OSINT and AI-phishing articles also address techniques central to Müller’s stated product remit. By contrast, the vendor comparisons are best classified as company-published analysis with an evident commercial context, not independent evaluations. Since the full texts are not supplied, it would be unwarranted to repeat their implied conclusions or describe them as original security research. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom))

## Conference presentations and interviews

**No conference presentation, speaking-program entry, interview transcript, or interview recording featuring revel8’s Tom Müller is established by the supplied sources.** The available material documents an author biography, article listings, company announcements, and funding coverage. A lack of evidence in this set is not evidence that he has never spoken publicly; it means that a date, venue, interviewer, or presentation title cannot responsibly be supplied here. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom); [revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m))

The name-matching issue is especially consequential for this category: a video about SpaceX co-founder **Tom Mueller** and a podcast hosted by crisis professional **Tom Mueller** are not evidence of talks or interviews by revel8’s Müller. Neither source links its subject to revel8. ([YouTube, n.d.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SVH9IS5a4ss); [*The Leading in a Crisis Podcast*, n.d.](https://www.leadinginacrisis.com/2175298/contributors/53730-tom-mueller))

## Recent company announcements and their relevance

### September 2025 seed financing

On **September 25, 2025**, Vestbee reported a **€5.7 million seed round** led by Peak, bringing revel8’s reported cumulative funding to **€7 million**. Revel8’s own announcement describes the same overall **€7 million** funding figure and says the proceeds would support product development and the expansion of its human-centered cybersecurity platform. Menlo Times also reports the €5.7 million seed amount and €7 million cumulative total, naming Fortino Capital and Merantix Capital among the participating investors. These are company-level financing facts; the sources do not specify Müller’s individual fundraising responsibilities. ([Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m); [revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [*Menlo Times*, n.d.](https://www.menlotimes.com/post/revel8-levels-up-its-fight-against-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

The distinction between **€5.7 million newly raised** and **€7 million total reported funding** is important: the figures describe different measures rather than two separate, equally sized announcements. Startup.eu’s displayed **€11.4 million** total appears alongside two entries for a **€5.7 million September 2025 seed round** and its conflicting 2026 founding date. On the supplied evidence, the duplicated listing is not a sound basis for claiming that revel8 completed two distinct €5.7 million rounds. ([Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m); [Startup.eu, n.d.](https://www.startup.eu/startup/revel8))

### Customers, distribution, and future plans

Revel8’s announcement names **FC Bayern, OBI, and Stihl** among its customers and says it planned to strengthen enterprise features and grow internationally. Menlo Times separately reports STACKIT marketplace availability. These announcements are pertinent to Müller because he is the company’s identified product lead, but neither source establishes his personal role in securing customers, arranging distribution, or completing later expansion plans. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom); [*Menlo Times*, n.d.](https://www.menlotimes.com/post/revel8-levels-up-its-fight-against-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

The funding announcement also describes revel8 as Berlin-headquartered and mentions a **planned relocation to Munich in early 2026**. The supplied material does not confirm whether that move occurred, so the announcement is evidence of a plan, not of a completed change of headquarters. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

## Evidence-based conclusion

As of **November 22, 2026**, the most defensible characterization of Tom C. Müller is that he is a **revel8 co-founder publicly identified by the company as its product lead**, whose documented remit covers realistic social-engineering simulations and interactive training, and who is credited with a series of 2026 articles on phishing, OSINT, fraud, training, and vendor selection. A third-party company database additionally labels him a co-CEO, but the company biography supplied here does not use that title. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom); [Tracxn, 2026](https://tracxn.com/d/companies/revel8/__y_4-TRqdVfYL7aJoS3_pcFUgSev2HB6U6ZT_96HodDY))

**My assessment is that his clearest publicly verifiable contribution is product direction and company-published explanation of AI-era social-engineering training—not an independently documented record of conference speaking or peer-reviewed technical research.** The €5.7 million seed announcement gives meaningful context for the scale of revel8’s announced plans, but it does not resolve the conflicting founding dates or establish the outcome of those plans. Keeping those limits explicit produces a more accurate professional profile than merging similarly named people or treating promotional claims as demonstrated results. ([revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/author-tom); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m); [revel8, n.d.](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))
